iconicAnchor.label: East Los Angeles vernacular commercial landscape
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The Smithsonian conversation identifies street vendors, temporary tables, vivid activity, hand-painted business signs, and commercial strips as a lived vernacular landscape rather than designed retail theater.

sources.title: On Fences, Plazas, and Latino Urbanism
sources.publisher: Smithsonian Center for Folklife and Cultural Heritage
supports: Street vendors, temporary tables and tarps, hand-painted signs, and social streetscapes form a community-authored vernacular commercial landscape.

sources.title: Festival of American Folklife 1990 Program Book
supports: The documented festival marketplace connects market vendors with making, selling, foodways, and public cultural exchange rather than treating a market as a decorative scene.
